stem:
Which of the following equation(s) is same as $2x^2 - 1 = 0$? (Note: $x \ne 0$)

$$\begin{array}{ll} \text{I.} & 3 - \left(\frac{1}{x^2} + 1\right) = 0 \\ \text{II.} & 2(x^2 - 1) = 0 \\ \text{III.} & \frac{1}{x} - 2x = 0 \end{array}$$
answer_review_note: Official key verified by independent mathematical solution.
explanation: Equation I: $3 - 1 - 1/x^2 = 0 \implies 2 - 1/x^2 = 0 \implies 2x^2 - 1 = 0$. Equation III: $1/x - 2x = 0 \implies (1 - 2x^2)/x = 0 \implies 2x^2 - 1 = 0$. Thus I and III are equivalent.
